patterns.title: Timers inside the process
patterns.why: Instances stop when idle and several can run at once, so a timer inside one fires late, never, or twice.
patterns.fix: Cloud Scheduler starts a Cloud Run job at the same times.
patterns.subject: the timers

patterns.title: Sessions kept in process memory
patterns.code: app.use(session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET, resave: false, saveUninitialized: false }));
patterns.why: Each instance has its own memory and loses it when it stops, so a user is signed out whenever a request lands on another instance or a new one.
patterns.fix: Signed cookies (cookie-session), with the key in Secret Manager.
patterns.subject: the sessions in memory

patterns.title: Files written to local disk
patterns.why: An instance's disk lives in its memory and is gone when the instance stops; other instances never see it.
patterns.fix: Write to a Cloud Storage bucket and hand out signed URLs.
patterns.subject: the files on disk

patterns.title: A worker waits on a Redis queue
patterns.why: Cloud Run gives an instance CPU only while it answers a request, so a worker waiting on Redis gets no CPU between requests and its jobs stall.
patterns.fix: Cloud Tasks: each job becomes a POST to /tasks/<name> on the service; retries and rate limits move to the queue.
patterns.subject: the worker

clean: SQLite or files used as a database
